scope: Copy/paste commands, exact-next-command handoffs, operator reports, scoped skills, and technician harness documentation.

rules.message: A duplicated PowerShell prompt was presented as executable input.
A PowerShell prompt prefix was presented as executable input.
A Command Prompt prefix was presented as executable input.
A PowerShell continuation prompt was presented as executable input.
PowerShell error-location output was presented as executable input.
PowerShell error metadata was presented as executable input.

rules.pattern: (?i)^\s*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*\s*:\s+(?:A positional parameter|The term|Cannot bind|Parameter set|Exception|An error occurred)\b
rules.message: PowerShell diagnostic output was presented as executable input.
Instructional prose was mixed into an executable command block.

presentationRequirements: Name the shell outside the code fence.
Put executable input only inside the code fence.
Begin the command at the first non-whitespace character; never include PS, CMD, WSL, tmux, or continuation prompts.
Never mix stdout, stderr, stack traces, transcript lines, or expected output into the command block.
Prefer a repository-owned CMD or PS1 entrypoint over a long inline bootstrap.
Carry fixed repository, ref, and SHA values into the command while leaving genuinely unknown runtime values explicit.
State the owner, dependency, expected artifact, and completion gate outside the command block.
proofCeiling: Proves that registered operator-facing command blocks and supplied candidate files are free of known prompt, continuation, transcript, and PowerShell error-output contamination. It does not prove the command succeeds on a workstation.
